name: Gurgi Mosque
subtitle: 1833 Ottoman-Karamanli mosque in the Medina of Tripoli, crowned by 16 domes on marble columns and an octagonal minaret.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: 16 domes on marble columns and octagonal minaret

parts.text: A celebrated Ottoman-era mosque located in the historic Medina of Tripoli near the Arch of Marcus Aurelius. Completed in 1833 by naval commander Mustafa Gurgi during the Karamanli dynasty, the mosque features a square prayer hall covered by a grid of 16 small domes supported by ancient marble spolia columns, an octagonal minaret with two carved balconies, and walls clad in polychrome ceramic tiles and delicate Andalusian-style stucco reliefs.

gaps: Primary waqf foundation deeds of the Gurgi family complex were not accessed directly.
